provenance: Scored by the write-up agent (Claude Code) from research notes 01-04 and the option material. The workflow's judge-panel output did not reach the write-up step, so this is a single-agent scoring: treat it as advisory, not as an independent panel.

criteria.label: Covers all spec modules F1-F5, 1-18 and the three differentiators
Tenant isolation, processor posture, DPA story (DM-6.8, ADR 0008, PDPL/GDPR/APP)
Reuse of what exists and fit with written rules/ADRs
Agent sessions to the complete product
Release coupling, blast radius, vendor/contract drift

rationale.A: Only A and B cover the full spec. A keeps the CRM's public surfaces, vendor webhooks, KMS decrypt and scrubber out of the CIS process and task role, has its own deploy guard (crm.job), and gives the DPA a clean technical annex. Cost: one more repo, ECS service and REST API (~1 extra session, ~$20/month on Dev).
rationale.B: Same coverage and cost as A and the most reuse, but CRM releases would be gated by CIS waves (DM-11.4), the CIS task role must read the crm_app secret, and CIS migrations are frozen until X1 S22. Weakest isolation story for a product whose selling point is privacy.
rationale.C: Cheapest and fastest, lowest AA exposure, but it is not the product Ms. Thư specified and contradicts the S245 decision. Kept as an export path inside A (crm.integration_link) for agencies that already run HubSpot/Zoho.

grafts: From B: the agent UI is served inside the portal host (Vercel multi-zone under portal.lumiguides.it.com/portal/crm) and reuses the portal UI kit by byte-copy guard, so tenants see one portal and one sign-in.
From B: keep the crm-NNN key space and owners.yaml entry exactly as ADR 0008 §8 planned, so nothing is renumbered.
From C: crm.integration_link + outbox export to HubSpot/Zoho/Pipedrive as a module (W7) for agencies that keep their own CRM; the intake + attribution path (W3) is useful on its own from day one.
From research 03: the 8 table-stakes items are acceptance checks for the W3/W5 demos with pilot agencies.
